verdict: All 15 acceptance criteria pass mechanically and by hand: node --check is clean, the ten pinned exports are present with the right arities and nothing extra, the six-row table matches the ratified numbers field-for-field (verified by script), weights sum to 100, effectiveRuns returns 2/1/3 for the three worked cases, 'ironback' greps to 0, none of the forbidden Garage identifiers appear, and every hit for Profile/Corp/Forge/RARITIES is inside a comment. The prose is genuinely at the bar: the PP_VEHICLE_NAMES non-merge is recorded as a costed rejected design, the condition table is labelled a MIRROR with index.html named as the authority and the drift consequence spelled out, lotSlots is a recorded non-enforcement with the sites named, the provisional numbers pre-write their own deletion, and auditRigs() is exported-not-run with the reason given. It also names a real legacy defect (the auction win path assigning slot = p.lot.length) and honestly labels it unmeasured; that defect is real at index.html:196915 and is independently corroborated by another builder's comment at index.html:80471. What stops this being a win is that the file's headline safety mechanism does not fire in the only place it is wired: auditRigs() guards its drift check with `typeof condMult === 'object'`, and the sole in-repo caller (src/transport/index.js:1239) hands it an arrow function, so the mirror drift alarm silently returns [] = sound. The header asserts a protection the assembled system does not have.
biggest_gap: auditRigs()'s condition-drift alarm is vacuous against its only real caller. src/transport/index.js:1239 calls auditRigs(ids, (c) => num(call(b.condMult, 1, c))) — a FUNCTION — while rigs.data.js:510 gates the whole drift block on `if (condMult && typeof condMult === 'object')`. typeof fn === 'function', so the block is skipped and [] is returned; I confirmed this by injecting a drifted Wrecked=0.25: passed as an object the audit reports the drift, passed as index.js's function it reports nothing. Fix inside the owned file: accept a lookup function as well as a map (probe each of the six PP_CONDITIONS keys through it), and — more importantly — push a problem string when condMult is absent or of an unusable shape, so an unfed alarm reads as 'not checked' instead of 'sound'. As written the file reproduces the exact inversion it warns about twelve lines earlier ('a stale fallback makes the corresponding rule pass VACUOUSLY, which is the direction that hides bugs').
evidence: AC verification: `node --check public/src/transport/rigs.data.js` passes.
